source.title: Explicitly Bayesian Regularizations in Deep Learning

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendix; no apparent cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: Tests random-label fitting with training and testing error, using a CNN on a new synthetic image dataset.
record.gate_note: Section 4.4 reports CNN3’s training and testing errors on random labels. Other random-label statements in the introduction and discussion describe cited work or the authors’ interpretation, not separate experiments.
record.test_reason: Section 4.4 repeats random-label classification with a standard CNN and measures training and testing error, directly testing V1 in a synthetic digit dataset.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the random-label conclusion: the CNN fits training labels but has testing error around 90%, which the authors attribute to the learned conditional label relationship rather than their proposed Bayesian regularization. Their broader conclusion is that early CNN layers represent input priors and therefore provide explicitly Bayesian regularization. Their statement about good generalization on random labels refers to estimating the input distribution, despite poor classification performance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a synthetic handwritten-digit dataset and CNN3, rather than the original study’s setting; the paper calls the experiment similar to the cited random-label experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 4 reports KL divergence 0.47 between the input distribution and the estimated first-layer distribution during random-label training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A CNN trained on random labels can retain an accurate estimate of the input's marginal distribution under the authors' probabilistic representation. This does not test the explicit regularizers named in V5.

record.problems: The random-label result is shown for one CNN and one synthetic dataset. No exact test-error value or uncertainty is reported, and the text does not establish that training hyperparameters were unchanged from true-label training.
record.rows_left_out: No separate numeric rows were recoverable from Figure 5 beyond the text-described outcomes in Section 4.4; no other claim-relevant results were reported.

untested.parts: The architecture is shared with the true-label experiments, but identical training hyperparameters are not documented; the random-label sampling procedure and experiment-specific optimizer settings are unspecified.
No matched convergence-time comparison or sweep over corruption fractions.
No fitting experiment on unstructured inputs. Gaussian samples are sorted and arranged using digit masks, producing spatially structured images.
No intermediate label-corruption fractions or test-error degradation curve.
No comparisons adding or removing weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation.
No measurement distinguishing when shared real patterns and noisy labels are learned.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. The figure's 200-epoch display does not establish V2 without a matched true-label convergence comparison. The authors' Bayesian interpretation does not challenge the observed random-label fitting result.

versions.untested_parts: Does not state whether training hyperparameters were unchanged from true-label training or report a matched true-label result for CNN3. The test-error result is described as around 90%, not given as an exact chance-level comparison.
